title: Toolchain checks
summary: `ty doctor` checks whether this machine can build and run the project. It reports only the toolchains (compilers and build tools) and controller runtimes that the project uses. `--json` prints the same report in a format for other programs. Each row is `ready`, `partial` (found, but too old or not complete), `missing`, or `info`. `info` is a tool that the project can do without: a native companion compiler (Swift, Kotlin, Rust or C# for a native target), TinyGo, or `wasm-opt`. Each native target that the project declares (a `bundle:<target>` script in `package.json`) adds `info` rows for the tools that build its app: `xcrun` for macos; `xcodebuild` and the iOS simulator SDK for ios; `ANDROID_HOME`, `gradle` and `javac` for android; `cl`, `rc.exe` and `TAC_WEBVIEW2_SDK` for windows; `cc` and the `gtk4` and `webkitgtk-6.0` libraries (through `pkg-config`) for linux. `ty doctor` exits with 0 when every needed toolchain is ready, and with 1 when a needed toolchain is missing or too old, or the project cannot be read. `info` rows do not change the exit status. A service that runs as WebAssembly needs these checks. TypeScript: `tsc` 6 or newer, from the project's `node_modules/.bin` or from PATH. Rust: the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target. Go: Go 1.27 or newer; TinyGo 0.42 or newer makes release modules several times smaller, and without it the build uses the standard Go compiler. C# and F#: the .NET `wasm-tools` workload (the row is named "C# services on the web"). Kotlin: `kotlinc-js` 2.1.10 and the kotlin-stdlib-wasm-js 2.1.10 `.klib` file from Maven Central; set `TAC_KOTLIN_WASM_STDLIB` to that file. Swift: Swift 6.3.3 from swift.org (not Xcode's `swiftc`) and the matching Swift SDK for WebAssembly from `swift sdk install`; set `TAC_SWIFT_WASM_SDK` to its `wasm32-unknown-wasip1` folder, and set `TAC_SWIFT_WASM_COMPILER` to the swift.org `swiftc` when another `swiftc` comes first on PATH. Kotlin and Swift show `partial` without `wasm-opt`, because their release modules would be much larger. Java: `javac` from a JDK 21 or newer and TeaVM 0.15.0. Dart: the Dart SDK 3.13 or newer. Ruby: Tachyon's Ruby WebAssembly runtime, which Tachyon builds once with Ruby, Emscripten 6.0.10 or newer (`emcc`) and a C compiler (`clang` on macOS, `gcc` elsewhere, or `CC`). Lua: Tachyon's Lua WebAssembly runtime, built once with Emscripten 6.0.10 or newer, and the `lua` program (5.4 or newer) for test units. When a runtime is already in the Tachyon cache, its row shows it as ready instead of the build tools. Python: the pinned Pyodide 314.0.7 runtime (CPython 3.14.2). Copy the five core files from the official `pyodide-core-314.0.7.tar.bz2` archive into the `python-web/314.0.7` folder of the Tachyon cache; ty checks the size and SHA-256 hash of each file and never downloads Python or Python packages. The project also needs `tac.python` in `client/manifest.json` with `"runtime": "pyodide-314.0.7"` and `"profile": "offline"`; without it the row shows `TY1605`. `wasm-opt` from Binaryen version_133 or newer makes the release WebAssembly of Rust, Go, Swift and Java smaller. For Yon, the report checks each runtime that the controllers use: `node`, or `bun` when `node` is not on `PATH` (`YON_JAVASCRIPT_RUNTIME`), `python3`, or `python` on Windows (`YON_PYTHON_RUNTIME`), `ruby` 3.3 or newer (`YON_RUBY_RUNTIME`), `java`, `groovyc` (Groovy 4 or newer, or `GROOVY_HOME`), `kotlinc`, `dotnet` for C# and F#, `rustc` and `cargo`, `dart`, `go` 1.27 or newer, `php-cgi` and `lua`. `ty doctor --install` offers to install each missing tool that Tachyon can install, the way `ty init` does (`--yes` installs them without asking). For TeaVM it downloads the five jars from Maven Central, checks each one against the SHA-256 that Tachyon pins, and keeps them in the Tachyon cache, never in the project. `TAC_TEAVM_HOME` still points at a folder of your own. Each check has its own time limit: 10 seconds, and 60 seconds for the C# check, because it builds a small project. So a busy machine does not report a working toolchain as broken. The development server and `ty test` run the same checks before they start. `ty --help` does not list `doctor`, but `ty doctor --help` prints its options and exit status.
